description: We exist at the intersection of binary logic and the living world. To us, Space Apps challenges are far more than logic puzzles—they are opportunities to give orbital observations a heartbeat, translating cold, space-borne telemetry into living, meaningful impact. We build at the edge where data meets reverence, driven by a simple, shared devotion: preserving the extraordinary, fragile biosphere.
summary: The Earth Information Jukebox, EmoEarth, developed by StarTrek transforms silent satellite telemetry into visceral orchestral performance. Built on a Python Flask backend to deliver responsive, and accessible experience, this multi-sensory application is crafted to empower blind and low-vision explorers to experience changing climate conditions. With keyboard shortcuts, users can control the narration, playback and real-time layer switching across an interactive 3D globe - exploring MODIS Terra polar ice surface temperature, ECCO2 ocean currents and sea temperature, and DYAMOND/GEOS atmospheric carbon dioxide. Users are able to retrieve fresh satellite datasets directly within the app. In this concert hall, the Earth itself is the composer. Powered by custom Python mathematical synthesizer, the sonification engine translates planetary telemetry into spatial hemisphere orchestration, chromatic instrumentation, and climate-driven tempo—turning rising thermal and emission trajectories into high-urgency string tremolos and brass swells. Because music alone conveys emotion and momentum rather than scientific context, EmoEarth integrates AI-driven voice-over narration pipeline using Google Gemini API. As users toggle between layers, the system generates vivid, immersive and tactile descriptions. Every shift in the orchestral score is anchored with grounded narration, weaving visual telemetry, spatial audio and spoken storytelling into a single cohesive sensory tapestry.
details:
🌍 EmoEarth: The Earth Information Jukebox

Developed by Team StarTrek

The Blind Spot in Open Science

Petabytes of NASA telemetry track every breath of our changing planet, yet traditional maps leave millions of blind and low-vision people in the dark. EmoEarth turns that blind spot into a symphony. Combining multi-source satellite data with expressive orchestral soundscapes, AI narration, and 3D spatial audio, EmoEarth transforms Earth observation from something you merely look at into something everyone can hear, feel, and experience.

Interactive Web App (Login as Guest): https://emoearth-awbchng6cce2aufp.malaysiawest-01.azurewebsites.net/

GitHub Link: https://github.com/LimWeeYip/EmoEarth/

(Short) Demo Video Link: https://youtu.be/UHlu16eFrH8?si=IzSmsCQxPb0w7GyX

(Full Video) Link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GcKnHnckvzQ

1. The Planetary Symphony: How EmoEarth Works

The web application has been tested and verified to be fully compatible with Chrome, Edge, and Safari on both macOS and Windows, as well as on iPhone (iOS 26.2 and 27.2) and Android (One UI 9.0).

On-Demand NASA Sync: Retrieve and integrate updated satellite datasets directly from NASA SVS/Worldview directly within the app

Tools and Languages

Python packages (see requirements.txt):

Multi-source Data Ingestion

Retrieval from open datasets: polar MODIS Terra Ice Surface Temperature (via NASA GIBS WMS), ECCO2 Global Sea Surface Currents and Temperature (NASA/GSFC SVS), and DYAMOND Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide.


Orchestral Synthesis Engine

Chromatic Instrumentation: Moving across the pixels in each frame, each magnitude serves dedicated orchestral section based on 7-color-bar bands. Deep cellos and basses play low magnitude while trumpet and timpani govern highest spikes. The loudness scales dynamically between frozen 5th and 95th percentiles to ensure consistency while keeping every voice alive.

Spatial Hemisphere Architecture: Northern Hemisphere layer magnitude shapes the two-octave violin melody, while Southern Hemisphere magnitude anchors the bass line—arranged across a realistic stereo concert stage (violins and harp left, violas and woodwinds center, cellos, basses, and trumpets right).

Harmonic Modulations, Tempo & Emotional Articulation: A 15-frame smoothed net trend governs key shifts between C major (I - vi - IV - V) and C minor (i - VI - iv - V with falling harp arpeggios), buffered by hysteresis thresholds (±0.05) and bridged seamlessly via a dominant G major pivot chord, timpani roll, and horn swell. Visual change velocity across the active layer drives tempo between 66 and 132 BPM (adding rapid two-note runs on sharp transitions), while valence and arousal classify each frame into one of six expressive states (Serene, Joyful, Triumphant, Melancholy, Tense, or Urgent) that reshape articulation from smooth legato to trembling string tremolos and urgent brass.

Pure Acoustic Physics in Code: Every section is sculpted mathematically—combining multi-player detuned wavetables with delayed vibrato, breath noise for flutes, decaying upper partials for plucked harp strings, bell partials for celesta, and mallet-struck drum modes for timpani—finished through a 2.4-second concert-hall convolution reverb and soft limiter.

2. Beyond Visuals: Universal Accessibility

Intuitive Climate Empathy: Science measures the storm, yet it rarely makes us feel the wind. By translating melting sea ice, warming oceans, and atmospheric shifts into nervous string tremolos, brass fanfares, and shifting harmonies, EmoEarth closes the distance between raw satellite data and human instinct—so you don't just observe a changing planet.

Radical Inclusion for Blind and Low-Vision Explorers: Traditional Earth science often exclusively relies on visual maps and color bars, excluding millions of visually impaired learners. EmoEarth turns climate telemetry into a rich spatial-auditory experience—complete with single-key shortcuts (Z, X, C for layers; D for AI narration; Space for playback) and spoken state changes.

Cloud-Ready Delivery: EmoEarth is engineered as a deployable web application featuring asset caching, authentication and guest access, and one-command Microsoft Azure deployment.

How the page plays the page

  • User arrives on intial login page. Option to enter email address or skip to access as guest.
  • Narration first (off by default; tick it in the playback bar): when you press ▶ from the beginning, the description is spoken first and the music starts when it ends, so the two never play over each other. Press ▶ (shown as ⏭) again to skip straight to the music. The box is off when EmoEarth opens; tick it to hear the description first (the browser remembers that choice, and unticking it again turns it off). 🗣 Describe or the D key plays the narration at any time.
  • 🗣 Describe button (or the D key): speaks the description at any time. If the music is playing, it keeps going quietly underneath (turned down to 15%) and comes back to full volume afterwards. Press it again or Esc to stop.
  • Caption: the description are shown at the top of the screen while they are spoken.

3. Behind the Curtain: Architecture & Tech Stack

  • Backend & Audio Synthesis: Python 3, Flask, NumPy (mathematical waveform & reverb synthesis), Pillow & OpenCV (satellite swath gap-filling & color-bar telemetry extraction), Pandas (waveform analytics), OWSLib & Requests (NASA GIBS API integration), lameenc & pyttsx3.
  • Frontend & 3D Graphics: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Three.js (3D planetary rendering), custom GLSL shaders (smooth multi-day texture interpolation), Web Audio API (AnalyserNode for 28-band real-time frequency visualization), and Web Speech API.
  • AI & Cloud Infrastructure: Google Gemini API (google-genai for automated tactile narration), Firebase Authentication, and Microsoft Azure App Services.
  • Development Environment: Visual Studio Code, Git, macOS and Windows workstations.

4. Where Astrophysics Meets Artistry: Creative Vision

Most Earth data projects stop at plotting pixels on a map. EmoEarth asks: What if planetary telemetry could be performed like a symphony? Combining classical music theory (voice-leading, pivot-chord modulations, orchestral seating) with real-time WebGL shaders and generative AI narration creates a rare synthesis of art, astrophysics, and inclusive design. Even our sign-in portal tells a story—animating NASA's Terra satellite sweeping across its polar orbit to paint surface temperatures in real time.

Multi-sensory UI design encompassing:

  • Dual-Hemisphere Telemetry Timeline: A synchronized time-series plot tracks Northern and Southern hemisphere trends side-by-side with a live playhead—visually mirroring the musical counterpoint between the higher-register violin melody (North) and the deep cello/bass foundation (South).
  • Live Musical Score Telemetry: Instead of treating music as background audio, the interface exposes the compositional logic in real time—displaying dynamic BPM/tempo (mapping velocity of climate change), key signature flashes (C major vs. C minor shifts on net trend reversals), and expressive remarks as environmental intensity swells or subsides.
  • Synthesized Waveform & Harmonic Equalizer: Driven by a Web Audio AnalyserNode, a 28-band live frequency equalizer and synthesized waveform visualizer translate pure numpy-generated audio physics into color-coded light—allowing users to literally watch deep polar bass and high solar treble pulse in sync with the 3D globe's emotional aura.
  • Atmospheric Mood Glow: The 3D globe and HUD dynamically shift their ambient lighting across six distinct emotional states (Serene, Joyful, Triumphant, Melancholy, Tense, Urgent), creating an immediate visual-emotional feedback loop that reinforces the orchestral mood.

5. Why EmoEarth Matters: Giving Our Planet a Voice

When a massive wildfire scars a forest or polar ice thins prematurely, Earth does not register a "statistical anomaly"—it experiences trauma. By translating NASA’s multi-layer Earth observations into a 7-part orchestral score and tactile AI narration, EmoEarth allows humanity to hear the planet’s grief, feel its fever, and celebrate its recovery.

Core impact pillars:

  • Radical Inclusion for Blind & Low-Vision Explorers: Traditional satellite portals lock millions of blind and visually impaired individuals out of Earth science. EmoEarth tears down that wall—combining expressive musical sentiments (where minor keys and trembling strings convey ecological stress) with vivid, spatial AI narration (narrate.py) and full keyboard navigation so every explorer can intimately feel the shape and mood of their home world.
  • Witnessing Our Footprint in Real Time: Watching a forest fire scar a continent or seeing summer ice vanish becomes deeply personal when the room fills with the quiet grief of a solo violin and trembling strings. EmoEarth turns abstract environmental timelines into a shared human memory, helping people recognize how our daily choices ripple across the biosphere.
  • A Universal Language Beyond Borders: Climate change affects every corner of the globe, yet scientific reports are often locked behind complex terminology and language barriers. Music needs no translation—joyful major swell or a mournful minor cadence evokes the exact same human emotion—allowing people from every culture and background to understand the Earth's story together.

🚀 Future Horizons & Real-World Opportunities

EmoEarth is built on a modular, cloud-ready architecture (Flask + Azure + Three.js), positioning it to grow far beyond a hackathon prototype into a global platform for education, science, and policy-making:

1. Inspiring the Next Generation of Stewards

Young children connect with the world instinctively through color, melody, and emotion. Brought into classrooms and science museums, EmoEarth translates planetary data into vibrant visuals and living music—letting children hear the heartbeat of the Earth, explore how oceans and ice protect one another, and build an intuitive, lifelong love for environmental science.

2. Real-Time Planetary Monitoring for Space Agencies

Space agencies like NASA, ESA, and JAXA capture terabytes of fresh satellite imagery every single day. EmoEarth’s ingestion pipeline can be connected directly to live orbital feeds—allowing scientists, educators, and the public to watch and listen to unfolding planetary events, from seasonal monsoons to sudden heatwaves, as they happen.

3. Listening for Hidden Climate Patterns

The human ear is remarkably good at catching subtle changes in rhythm, tension, and harmony—often noticing patterns that our eyes gloss over on a crowded map. Over time, EmoEarth’s sonification engine can help researchers scan decades of archival satellite data simply by listening for unexpected shifts in the planet’s musical score.

🤖 Use of AI in Development

Transparency and responsible AI collaboration played a key role in bringing EmoEarth from concept to reality—both inside the application and across our engineering workflow:

  • In-App Accessibility Narration (Google Gemini): Embedded directly into EmoEarth’s core pipeline (narrate.py), Gemini translates daily planetary telemetry and visual metrics into vivid, tactile spoken descriptions, ensuring universal accessibility for all explorers.
  • Code Architecture & Debugging (Claude): Assisted in structuring Python synthesis logic, refining numpy audio generation pipelines, and troubleshooting complex synchronization and deployment bugs.
  • Domain Synthesis & Literature Review (Google Gemini): Accelerated research into NASA Earth observation terminology, satellite layer specifications (GIBS, ECCO2, DYAMOND), and existing climate sonification projects.
  • Documentation & Editorial Polish (Claude & Google Gemini): Cross-checked technical documentation, README clarity, and project descriptions to ensure scientific accuracy and clear, human-centered storytelling.
